quotes.text: It is the communion of the human soul with Divinity.

quotes.text: Thus the niyamas are the virtues which calm the disturbed mind, leading towards peace both within and around the sadhaka.
quotes.relevance: This quote emphasizes the role of Niyama in bringing inner peace and harmony, aligning with the idea of self-purification rules in yoga.

quotes.relevance: This quote gives a practical guidance on practicing yoga to merge the practitioner's body, mind, and intelligence with the Self.

quotes.text: These three streams of jñana, karma and bhakti flow into the river of Yoga and lose their identity. Thus the path of Yoga alone takes every type of sadhaka, from the dull (mudha) to the restrained (niruddha), towards freedom and beatitude.

quotes.text: Chitta and prana are in constant association. Where there is chitta there prana is focused, and where prana is there chitta is focused.
quotes.relevance: This fact emphasizes the interconnectedness of chitta (consciousness) and prana, another main idea of the chapter.

quotes.text: If breath (prana) prevails, then the desires are controlled, the senses are held in check and the mind is stilled.
quotes.relevance: This quote illustrates the power of prana in controlling desires and calming the mind, which aligns with the key concept of using pranayama to control and harness prana.

quotes.relevance: This quote provides practical guidance for Pranayama practice, emphasizing the importance of correct posture and relaxation.

quotes.text: The light of intelligence is lit simultaneously in the brain as well as in the mind. This leads to right living, right thinking, quick action and sound judgement.

quotes.text: To reach this inner light he turns to meditation or dhyana.

quotes.text: The practice of meditation brings it to a state of stability and then directs it to proceed from imperfect knowledge to perfection.
quotes.relevance: This quote is related to the main idea that meditation improves the practitioner's state of mind and knowledge.

quotes.text: Only people who are easily dejected or distressed and who have dull or weak minds are advised to direct the gaze at the centre between the eyebrows with closed eyes for short periods of time. This practice brings about mental stability and intellectual sharpness.
quotes.relevance: This quote is related to the main idea of the importance of proper eye positioning during meditation and its impact on mental stability and intellectual sharpness.

quotes.text: Stop meditation the moment the body starts swaying forwards, backwards or sideways or if faintness is felt. Do not persist when this happens, as it means that the time for meditation is over for the day.

quotes.text: In meditation the mind traces its origin and comes to rest there as a child rests on the lap of the mother.
quotes.relevance: This quote expresses the philosophical wisdom of meditation as a means to trace the origin of the mind and find personal spiritual haven.

quotes.text: Meditation abolishes the polarity between the analytical dominant consciousness of the front brain and the receding subconsciousness.
quotes.relevance: This quote relates to the theme of meditation's ability to bridge the gap between conscious and subconscious mind.

quotes.text: In meditation mind and matter are fused. This fusion burns out all distracting thoughts.
quotes.relevance: This quote explains how sustained meditation can lead to a fusion of mind and matter, hence enhancing creativity and energy.

quotes.text: Where there is Yoga, There is prosperity, success, freedom, and bliss.
quotes.relevance: This is a statement of the transformative power of yoga, one of the central themes in the literature.

quotes.text: Strength is more than the transformation of matter into other forms of matter, it is the transformation of the whole cycle of air and light into matter and back again.
quotes.relevance: This describes the transformative power of yoga, turning matter into energy and vice versa for human healing and invigoration.

quotes.text: It will also teach us to respect those elements which we have treated with such contempt- air, water and light- without which life cannot survive.
quotes.relevance: This quote highlights the significance of respect for elements like air, water, and light in the practice of yoga.

quotes.text: 'Yoga i s nothing but the total experience of human life ; it is a science of the integral man!'
quotes.relevance: This quote provides a philosophical understanding of yoga as a science of integral human experience.

quotes.text: Knowledge without action, and action without knowledge do not help man. They must be intermingled. So samkhya and Yoga go together.
quotes.relevance: This quote speaks to the importance of integrating knowledge and action in Yoga practice.

quotes.text: As all the parts put together become a tree, so all the eight stages put together form Yoga.
quotes.relevance: This statement emphasizes the interconnectedness of the eight stages of yoga.

quotes.text: Prana is the energy permeating the universe at all levels. It is physical, mental, intellectual, sexual, spiritual and cosmic energy. All vibrating energies are prana.
quotes.relevance: This quote perfectly encapsulates the concept of prana as life-giving energy permeating the universe, which is one of the main ideas in this chapter.

quotes.text: It also regulates all the sadhaka's thoughts, desires and actions, gives poise and the tremendous will-power needed to become a master of oneself.
quotes.relevance: This quote is motivational, emphasizing the power of Pranayama in self-mastery and regulation of thoughts, desires, and actions.

quotes.text: The body is compared to a pot. Like an unbaked earthen pot, the physical body wears away. Bake it hard in the fire of pranayama to gain stability.
quotes.relevance: This evocative quote illustrates the transformative power of pranayama, aligning with the main idea that pranayama can lead to changes in mental attitude and physical health.

quotes.text: We all breathe, but how many of us do so correctly, with attention?
quotes.relevance: This quote encapsulates the idea of the need for mindfulness and attention in breathing, a main theme in the text.

quotes.text: It gives delight to the sadhaka when prana enters it and swallows time.
quotes.relevance: This quote is inspiring as it conveys the spiritual delight one experiences when prana, the life force, flows through the susumna nadi.

quotes.text: When the kundalini energy reaches the sahasrara, the sadhaka has crossed all barriers and becomes an emancipated soul.
quotes.relevance: This quote speaks to the ultimate goal of yoga and spiritual practice - becoming an 'emancipated soul' or achieving self-realization.

quotes.text: Initially the guru brings himself down to the level of his pupil, whom he encourages and gradually lifts up by precept and example.
quotes.relevance: This quote illustrates the role of a guru in guiding a pupil through the process of spiritual growth and self-realization.

quotes.text: The guru is always alert to find a way to guide his intense pupil to realise his highest potential until he becomes a realised soul (siddha). The guru is always happy with his pupil, who may eventually surpass him.
quotes.relevance: This quote highlights the importance of the student-teacher relationship in spiritual growth.

quotes.text: Spiritual training (sadhana) has nothing to do with theoretical study, but it leads to a new way of life.
quotes.relevance: This quote emphasizes the practical, experiential nature of spiritual training over purely theoretical study.

quotes.text: When he realises that he is a spark of the Divine Flame burning throughout the universe, then all his past impressions (samskaras) are burnt out, and he becomes enlightened.
quotes.relevance: This statement encapsulates the idea of realization of one's identity as part of the divine as a key aspect of enlightenment.

quotes.text: It is the state of mind of the eater that is important. Yet a diet consisting of sattvic food only will help the practitioner to maintain a clear and unwavering mind.
quotes.relevance: This quote emphasizes both the importance of the eater's state of mind and the role of sattvic food in promoting health and calmness.

quotes.text: Yoga is not for those who gorge themselves, starve or sleep or stay awake too much.
quotes.relevance: This quote emphasizes the concept of moderation and discipline in yoga practice.

quotes.text: To continue and maintain his training, the pupil needs faith, virility, memory, meditation (sarn.adhi) and acute insight (praj.ii a ).
quotes.relevance: This quote provides practical guidance on the qualities needed for continuing and maintaining yoga training.

quotes.text: When pranayama is performed properly diseases disappear and a radiant state of well-being, enlightenment and serenity is experienced.
quotes.relevance: This quote encapsulates the role of pranayama in achieving serenity and self-realization. It also highlights the health benefits of correct pranayama practice.

quotes.text: If they are activated in coordination, courage comes to inspire the mind.
quotes.relevance: This quote is inspirational and speaks to the power of yoga practice to inspire courage and mental strength.

quotes.text: The right type acts like a real friend, teaching fresh adjustments and adaptations, continually molding the brain as well as the body.
quotes.relevance: This quote is motivational and emphasizes the significance of adjustments and adaptations in a yoga practice.

quotes.text: When practising pranayama, the yogi bows his head low, adjusting the position of the front in relation to the back of the skull in order to make himself humble.
quotes.relevance: This quote is inspiring as it incorporates the concept of humility in yoga practice.

quotes.text: Breath is like a turbulent river which, when harnessed by dams and canals, will provide abundant energy.
quotes.relevance: This quote is inspirational and provides a metaphorical understanding of the power of controlled breath in pranayama, resonating with the main ideas.

quotes.text: The practitioner is then known as a celibate (urdhvareta). Having mastered the sexual urge naturally but not by force, he stops dissipating his virility. He is fully potent yet a master of himself.
quotes.relevance: This quote highlights the necessity of a guru's guidance in sublimating the practitioner's increased power, which comes with mastering the bandhas.

quotes.text: The action of the consciousness in respiration is like that of a mother absorbed in watching her child at play. Though outwardly passive, she is mentally alert, observing him minutely while remaining completely relaxed.
quotes.relevance: This quote provides a philosophical perspective on the mindfulness required in yoga practice.

quotes.text: Inhale and exhale systematically with close attention to the rhythmic pattern of breath, as a spider symmetrically weaves its web and moves to and fro along it.
quotes.relevance: This quote provides practical guidance on the methodology of breath control in yoga.

quotes.text: Kumbhaka keeps the sadhaka silent at the physical, moral, mental and spiritual levels.
quotes.relevance: This quote encapsulates the concept of Kumbhaka as a state of suspense that can silence various levels of existence, aligning with the second main idea.

quotes.text: Knowledge of the bandhas is essential for the proper practice of kumbhaka. They act as safety valves for distributing, regulating and absorbing energy, and prevent its dissipation.
quotes.relevance: This quote speaks to the necessity of the bandhas in pranayama practice, which is one of the main ideas of the text.

quotes.text: As one uses tweezers to remove a thorn and feels freedom from pain at once, use the intelligence as the tweezers to remove faulty grips and movements which act as thorns in practice.
quotes.relevance: This quote emphasizes the role of self-awareness and self-correction in yoga practice.

quotes.text: The body is the kingdom. The skin is its frontier. Its ruler is the Atman, whose all seeing eye (jñana chaksu) watches every detail during pranayama.
quotes.relevance: This quote highlights the importance of self-awareness in yoga practice, and it metaphorically corresponds to the harmonious balance of body, mind, and intellect.

quotes.text: Very often, understanding and practice do not go together. One sadhaka may be better able to understand, while another may have better skill in practice. In each case, he has to develop uniformity in skill and intelligence and use them harmoniously for the better practice of pranayama.
quotes.relevance: This quote stresses the need for harmonizing understanding and practice in pranayama.

quotes.text: The sadhaka is lost in his ecstasy, but his experience of pranayama is purely subjective. He alone listens to the subtle and soft sound of his own breathing and enjoys the absolute soundless state of kumbhaka.
quotes.relevance: This quote portrays the personal and subjective nature of the yoga experience, tying into the theme of personal spiritual experience.

quotes.text: AUM is the word that all the Vedas glorify, and all self-sacrifice expresses. It is the goal of all sacred studies and the symbol of holy life.
quotes.relevance: This quote highlights the profound significance of AUM in spiritual studies, aligning with the main ideas of the text.

quotes.text: At first the pupil will find it hard to maintain rhythm during rechaka, bahya kumbhaka and puraka, as gasping will ensue. But it all eases with long and uninterrupted practice.
quotes.relevance: This quote emphasizes the importance of long and uninterrupted practice in pranayama, one of the main ideas of the text.

quotes.text: The path of visamavrtti pranayama is fraught with danger. So do not practise it on your own without the personal supervision of an experienced guru.
quotes.relevance: This quote highlights the potential risks of pranayama without proper guidance, supporting the main idea that pranayama should be practiced under the guidance of an experienced guru.

quotes.text: Remember Svarmarama's words in his Hatha Yoga Pradipika, that prana should be tamed more gradually than lions, elephants and tigers; otherwise it will kill the practitioner.
quotes.relevance: This quote emphasizes the need for gradual practice in taming prana, highlighting the main idea about the importance of gradual progress in pranayama.

quotes.text: This enables him to receive the incoming breath as life's elixir and a blessing from the Lord, and the outgoing breath as his surrender to Him.
quotes.relevance: This quote connects to the theme of the role of breath in connecting the practitioner with divine energy. It portrays breath as a gift and a surrender to a higher power.

quotes.text: If the flow is smooth and almost inaudible to the sadhaka, he will be filled with humility. This is the beginning of self-culture (Atma-sadhana).
quotes.relevance: This quote touches on the themes of the significance of humility and self-culture in yoga practice. It suggests that proper technique can lead to personal growth.

quotes.text: Stop the practice the moment irritation or strain is felt.
quotes.relevance: This quote provides practical advice on when to stop pranayama practice, relating to the main idea of potential dangers and precautions associated with pranayama.

quotes.text: Adjust the fingers on the nostrils delicately to control the volume and to regulate the flow of the out-breath evenly on both sides.
quotes.relevance: This quote offers practical guidance on pranayama technique, relating to the main idea of detailed guidelines for pranayama practice.
